text:
alex: quick proposal up: consider a small, router-first API shape that prefers gRPC internally but accepts JSON over HTTP at the edge for third-party clients. see sketch: https://stash/redwood/rt/proposals/router-first.md :thinking:

nina: link? can't access the PR from mobile. high-level: is this trying to avoid a full gateway transcode layer?

alex: yeah — goal is to avoid per-tenant transcoding hot paths. idea is: 1) runtime routes based on `Accept` header 2) edge ingresses do lightweight acceptance + auth, then forward proto*/grpc to internal services. fallback to JSON only for legacy partners.

matt: sounds cleaner than full transcode. what about telemetry/quotas? our console expects tokens-per-route and shape-based billing (embedding vs chat). how do we keep consistent metrics if we have two transport shapes?

sarah: we can canonicalize at the router: emit a unified `route.operation` metric and add a `transport` tag (grpc|json). console can keep the same per-route dashboards and add a transport breakdown. cheaper than changing all downstream services.

alex: exactly. pseudocode for policy blob i slapped together:```yaml
routing:
  match:
    - path: "/v1/generate"
      accept: ["application/grpc", "application/json"]
      route: generate.svc
      canonicalize: true
      metrics: {emit: ["route.operation", "token.count"]}
      quota_key: "client_id"
```

matt: couple concerns: 1) canonicalize step adds CPU at the router, could be a perf hotspot. 2) KV of `token.count` needs to map JSON tokens <-> grpc tokens consistently. we have to define tokenization rules upfront or we get billing variance.

nina: agree on tokenization rule. also we should keep a small, stable sampling signal to validate parity (e.g., sample 0.5% of json requests and forward to downstream as if they were grpc to compare outputs/latency). that helps consoles show regression alerts.

infra-bot: NOTE: rolling canaries are scheduled on infra-relay cluster for next deploy window (canary-size=5%).

sarah: rollout UX in console: add a single toggle on the route page "accept json fallback" with a tooltip that lists telemetry consequences (extra router cpu, transport tag in dashboards). also show a sample parity diff panel (from nina's sampling).

alex: ops plan: (1) implement canonicalize + transport tag (router) (2) add tokenization spec + test harness (matt/nina) (3) console UX toggle + sample-diff panel (sarah) (4) canary 5% on infra-relay (infra). agree? :rocket:

matt: sounds good. I'll prototype tokenizer and push a tiny benchmark (p99) against the router.

nina: i'll write the sampling harness and a short eval to alert if output-delta > 0.2 BLEU-ish for structured outputs.

sarah: i'll mock the console panel and put a toggled wireframe in figma then link in the RFC.

alex: thanks all — i'll open the RFC and tag you. merging notes: limit JSON fallback to known clients via `allowlist` in the blob until we validate.

matt: one more: please add `quota_key` propagation header `x-rw-quota` so downstream can verify charges if needed.

alex: added to RFC checklist. closing for now, will ping when RFC lands.
